item.title: NPR: Can Trump's economic war against Iran do what airstrikes and negotiations couldn't?
item.description: What a new round of U.S. sanctions could mean after nearly six months of war with Iran — and years of economic pressure on the country.

item.title: BBC News: Iran says it is 'fully prepared' to counter widened US economic sanctions
item.description: The US calls its latest sanctions on Iran an "economic D-Day", but Tehran says it has a plan to address them.

item.title: Al Jazeera: What would justice look like if there were no Rohingya left in Myanmar?
item.description: Nine years after the 2017 atrocities, Rohingya are still being forced to flee because the genocide has never stopped.

item.title: Ars Technica: AI is hitting entry-level jobs hardest, Stanford study finds
item.description: Young employment in AI-impacted fields down 19% compared to more AI-resistant occupations.

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: How Teen ‘After-Prom’ Kings in LA Monetized the High School Rager
item.description: The West Coast house-party scene has long been iconic. For these young, tech-savvy entrepreneurs, it was also inspiration for MyPlots, a party-promotion empire.

item.title: WIRED Science: Border Wall Construction Threatens 6,000 Years of History on Private Lands
item.description: Archeologists are confronting an “unfathomable” loss as border wall construction is set to cut across ranches that are home to unique historical sites, many of which haven’t been fully studied.

item.title: WIRED Business: It Should Be Harder to Apply for a Job. No, Really
item.description: Thanks to a dwindling supply of open roles, “one-click” applications, and the rise of artificial intelligence, it’s easier than ever to apply for a job. We’re all paying the price.
